answer: An agent marketplace can weight votes by tokens locked for 90 days, rather than by account count. The locked stake is the anchor: splitting 100 tokens among a thousand identities still buys only 100 tokens of voting weight, making headcount a relic of weaker designs. To gain influence, an attacker must buy and immobilize more tokens, sacrificing liquidity and other returns; spawning accounts alone cannot create a spiral of free voting power.
